title: Not one became mine
takeaway: Sometimes the people closest to you watch you burn and laugh.
scene: The poet describes his heart as a poor man's hut. Someone he loved set it on fire, and the people around him just watched.

original: میرے دل غریب دا جھگا ساڑ دتا محبوب دلدار میرے
سڑدا او ویکھ کے آہلنا رہے ہسدے اگے پچھے سی جینے وی یار میرے
transliteration: Mere dil gareeb da jhugga saar ditta mehboob dildaar mere
Sarda o vekh ke aahlna rahe hasde agge pichhe si jinne vi yaar mere
translation: My beloved, my darling, burned down the hut of my poor heart.
Seeing my nest burn, all my friends around me just kept laughing.
couplets.story: The person he loved most is the one who hurt him most. His heart was humble, like a little hut, and they burned it down. Worse, his friends saw it happen and laughed.

original: میری سدھراں دا جیڑا خون ہویا اتھرو رہے وگدے زارو زار میرے
احمدؔ اک نہ اپنا بن سکیا دشمن بن گئے کئی ہزار میرے
transliteration: Meri sadhraan da jehra khoon hoya, atthru rahe vagde zaaro zaar mere
Ahmad ik na apna ban sakiya, dushman ban gaye kayi hazaar mere
translation: Every hope of mine was killed, and my tears kept pouring down.
Ahmad, not a single one became truly mine, while thousands became my enemies.
couplets.story: All his dreams were crushed, and he couldn't stop crying. He ends with a sad truth: he couldn't win over even one person who was truly on his side, but he made thousands of enemies without trying.

deeper: This is mostly a poem about betrayal, and nothing in it names God. A Sufi reader could still hear a lesson in it. When every human friend fails you, the heart is pushed to look for the One who never does. That reading is possible, but it is the reader's, not something the poem says.
why: It's about betrayal and loneliness: feeling surrounded by people and still alone.
prompt: Who has stayed loyal to you when it mattered? Have you told them?
